{"rule":"Return this JSON object with the rule field unchanged and, in the text field, an original fictional passage of about 250 words that comes immediately BEFORE the current text in the same invented story.","text":"The rain began just after supper, ticking against the kitchen window while Mara’s mother sorted the mail. She made two piles: bills for the drawer and everything else for the counter. One cream-colored envelope, printed with the name of the neighborhood clinic, she set apart.

“I need to call them tomorrow,” she said, turning it over in her hands. “They’ve got the wrong date for your appointment.”

Mara was at the table, trying to make a pencil sketch of the streets around their house. Mr. Bell had mentioned the history assignment that afternoon, though he wouldn’t hand out the instructions until morning. She drew their block from memory: the corner shop, the bus stop, the narrow lane behind the library. At the edge of the page, she left a blank space where her grandmother had once said a footbridge used to cross the creek.

“Was it near the old mill?” Mara asked.

Her mother glanced up from the envelope. “You’ll have to ask Grandma. I was little when they took it down.”

Mara wrote ASK GRANDMA beside the blank space. Then she rubbed out the word, because it made the map look untidy, and promised herself she’d remember.

Her mother tucked the envelope beneath the grocery receipts. The phone rang, and she went into the hallway to answer it, speaking in a low voice about a shift swap. When she came back, she looked tired but smiled at Mara’s drawing.

“Bed soon,” she said. “I’ve got an early start.”

Mara gathered her pencils, folded the sketch, and left it beside her schoolbag. Beyond the window, the rain thickened until the streetlights shone like blurred coins. In the morning, she thought, she would ask about the bridge."}
